# Story 15.2: Launch the packaged server with an explicit non-dev NODE_ENV and verify dev-only features don't break

Status: done

## Story

As a developer,
I want `apps/electron/src/main.ts` to launch the packaged server child with an explicit non-dev `NODE_ENV`,
So that auth/CSRF are enforced in shipped builds while dev-only features keep working under genuine development (P0 item #2 from Aspect 9 of the critical review).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Story 15.1's red-phase tests pass: the packaged launch path sets an explicit non-dev `NODE_ENV` (`production` or a dedicated `'desktop'`) on the forked server child instead of defaulting to `'development'`.
2. Under that non-dev `NODE_ENV`, `auth.ts`'s `isDevEnvironment()` returns false and `shouldSkipAuth` does NOT skip JWT validation for all routes — auth/CSRF enforcement is active in the shipped build.
3. Genuine development/test runs keep their dev behavior: when a real developer launches with an explicit dev `NODE_ENV`, dev-only features (e.g., relaxed auth, debug endpoints) still work as before.
4. The previously-skipped tests from Story 15.1 are unskipped (`.skip()` removed) and pass; the full relevant suite is green with no pre-existing test modified, weakened, or removed.

- [x] Task 3 (AC: #2): Confirm auth/CSRF enforcement under non-dev.
  - [x] 3.1 Verify `apps/server/src/app/plugins/auth.ts`'s `isDevEnvironment()` returns false and `shouldSkipAuth` does not skip JWT validation for all routes when the child runs with the new non-dev `NODE_ENV`.

  - [x] 4.1 Confirm that a real developer launch with an explicit dev `NODE_ENV` still gets dev-only features; do not break the dev path by over-broadening the non-dev default.

  - [x] 5.1 Run the relevant test target(s) and confirm fully green with Story 15.1's tests now passing (unskipped).

## Dev Notes

- **Why:** `apps/electron/src/main.ts:107-108` defaults the forked server child's `NODE_ENV` to `'development'`, and `auth.ts`'s `isDevEnvironment()` (dev/test/local) makes `shouldSkipAuth` skip JWT validation for ALL routes in that mode — so the shipped desktop app runs with zero API authentication. This is P0 item #2 from Aspect 9.
- **First task is always unskip → confirm red → implement.** The red-phase tests from Story 15.1 define the target; do not edit their assertions to make them pass, only the production code.
- **Do not break genuine dev:** the fix must distinguish "packaged launch with no NODE_ENV" (→ non-dev) from "developer explicitly set a dev NODE_ENV" (→ keep dev behavior). A dedicated `'desktop'` value may be cleaner than reusing `production`.
- Vitest is the workspace test framework; server tests run via `nx test server`.

### Project Structure Notes

- Modify: `apps/electron/src/main.ts` (lines 107–108 — non-dev default for packaged launch).
- Possibly modify: `apps/server/src/app/plugins/auth.ts` (only if the new `'desktop'` value needs to be excluded from `isDevEnvironment()`'s dev set).
- Modify: Story 15.1's specs (remove `.skip()` markers only — no assertion changes).

### Completion Notes List

- Resumed from a prior interrupted run of this same story: uncommitted changes already existed in exactly the three files named by the Project Structure Notes (main.ts default flip, both specs unskipped). Per task, each was read and verified against its AC before acceptance — no rewrites were needed; all five tasks resolved as verification passes over that scaffold.
- Task 1 (AC #1–#3): removed every `it.skip` marker from Story 15.1's specs (`apps/electron/src/main.spec.ts`, `apps/server/src/app/plugins/auth-launch-env.spec.ts`) — skip-marker and comment updates only, no assertion changes (verified via per-file diff). Red confirmed live against the original code: electron AC #1 failed on `'development'` being in the dev set; server AC #2 failed with `authenticateJWT` never called under the launch-defaulted NODE_ENV.
- Task 2 (AC #1): `apps/electron/src/main.ts` now defaults the forked server child's `NODE_ENV` to `'production'` when absent, instead of `'development'`. Chose `'production'` over a dedicated `'desktop'` value: it is already outside `isDevEnvironment()`'s dev set (`development`, `test`, `local`), so no change to `auth.ts` was needed — smallest working diff. The guard remains `if (!childEnv['NODE_ENV'])`, so an explicit value always wins.
- Task 3 (AC #2): verified by reading `apps/server/src/app/plugins/auth.ts`: with `NODE_ENV=production`, `isDevEnvironment()` is false, so `shouldSkipAuth` reduces to the health-check check only and `authenticateJWT` runs for all other routes. The unskipped server spec proves this behaviorally (unauthenticated non-health request → 401 via JWT validation).
- Task 4 (AC #3): dev path preserved by construction — the default applies only when NODE_ENV is absent in the child env; a developer launching with an explicit `NODE_ENV=development` keeps relaxed auth. Pinned by the unskipped electron AC #2 test, which asserts the assignment stays guarded by the "value absent" check and that an explicitly set value is preserved.
- Task 5 (AC #4): green confirmed live — electron: 8/8 files passed (36 passed | 5 skipped; the 5 skips are a pre-existing smoke spec's runtime graceful skip when build artifacts are absent, unrelated to this story); server: 84/84 files passed. No pre-existing test modified, weakened, or removed.
- Environment note: first local server run showed 10 extra failing suites from a missing generated Prisma client (`Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default'` — `postinstall` only generates under CI). Fixed with `pnpm exec prisma generate`; after that the only red test was this story's AC #2.
- Quality gate: `pnpm all` green (lint + build + unit tests with coverage for affected projects electron and server, exit 0).
